questions.question: What does the {id} in @GetMapping("/doctors/{id}") represent?
options: A template variable that captures part of the URL path
A field in the JSON body
questions.explanation: Curly braces in a mapping create a slot, and @PathVariable reads the value that fills it.

questions.question: When should you prefer a path variable over a query parameter?
options: To identify one specific item such as a doctor with a given id
To pass an optional sort order
To send a large JSON document
To set the response content type
questions.explanation: Path variables identify a resource, and query parameters are better for optional filters, sorting and paging.

questions.question: The mapping is @GetMapping("/doctors/{id}") with @PathVariable int id. A client calls GET /doctors/abc. What happens?
options: Status 400 Bad Request, and the method does not run
questions.explanation: Spring cannot convert abc to an int, so it answers 400 before calling the method.

questions.question: For @GetMapping("/wards/{ward}/beds/{bed}") the client calls GET /wards/B/beds/12. Which values do ward and bed receive?
questions.explanation: The slots are filled in order from the path, so ward gets B and bed gets 12.

questions.question: A mapping is @GetMapping("/patients/{patientId}") and the method is patient(@PathVariable String id), compiled without parameter names kept. What is the fix?
options: Write @PathVariable("patientId") so the names are linked explicitly
questions.explanation: When the Java name differs from the slot name, name the slot inside the annotation so Spring can link them.
